art.subject: Mongolian Lark (Melanocorypha mongolica), adult (sexes similar, female duller with smaller breast patches), as seen in Korea in late autumn: crown chestnut, often with a paler buff centre; broad whitish supercilium; chestnut nape; throat white; a large black patch on each side of the upper breast, sometimes nearly joining into a band; mantle and scapulars warm brown with dark streaks and buff fringes; lesser and median wing coverts chestnut; secondaries largely white, showing as a white panel on the folded wing; breast and belly white with a rufous-buff wash on the flanks; tail dark brown with white outer feathers; heavy pale yellowish-horn bill; dark eye; pinkish-brown legs.
art.pose: standing upright on bare ground among dry stubble, side view
art.scene: dry harvested farmland with stubble and bare earth in Korea in late autumn, clear cold light; no people, buildings or text
art.build: A large, heavy-bodied lark, clearly larger and bulkier than a Eurasian Skylark and close to a White-cheeked Starling in size, with a big head and no crest. Bill thick, deep-based and conical, almost finch-like, shorter than the head. Legs medium, pinkish-brown; walks on the ground with a fairly upright stance. Tail rather short and square. In flight the broad wings show white secondaries forming a broad white trailing edge to the inner wing, contrasting with chestnut coverts and dark primaries; the tail shows white outer feathers.
avoid: Do not paint a slim, crested, streaky-breasted lark (Eurasian Skylark); this species is bulky, crestless and unstreaked white below.
Do not omit the large black patches on the sides of the breast or the chestnut crown and nape.
Do not make the bill thin or dark; it is thick, conical and pale.
Do not paint all-brown wings; the secondaries are mostly white.
